title: Beeswax tealights
subtitle: Twelve pure beeswax tealights for holders and lanterns
excerpt: Pure beeswax tealights poured into aluminium tealight cups. Beeswax burns cleaner and longer than paraffin tealights, with a faint natural honey scent. No added fragrance, the beeswax scent is enough. Makes twelve tealights; each burns for around 4 hours.
sourceNotes: Beeswax tealight method: melt point 62-65°C; pour temperature 70°C for tealight cups to prevent a hollow centre. Tealight wicks: waxed cotton wicks pre-tabbed to aluminium tealight cups. Yield: standard aluminium tealight cup holds approximately 16 g of wax; 200 g of beeswax gives 12 tealights. Burn time: pure beeswax tealights burn approximately 4 hours each versus 3 hours for paraffin equivalents.

recipe.yieldDescription: 12 tealights (~16 g each; ~4-hour burn time per tealight)
recipe.batchNotes: Scale directly. 1 kg of beeswax gives approximately 60 tealights. Make large batches for best economy, beeswax is priced by weight.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Tealights are ready to use 2 hours after pouring, once fully set. They keep indefinitely.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Beeswax tealights last indefinitely. A white bloom may develop on the surface, natural wax crystallisation, harmless. Buff with a soft cloth if desired.

glossaryTerms.definition: The temperature at which melted beeswax is poured into tealight cups. At 70°C the wax is fluid enough to fill the small cup and release air bubbles before setting.

content.text: Pure beeswax tealights poured into standard aluminium cups. No added fragrance, beeswax has its own faint honey-wax scent that fills a room gently when burning. They burn longer than paraffin equivalents (around 4 hours each versus 3) and with less soot. Twelve tealights from 200 g of beeswax.

items.prepNote: yellow or white beeswax pastilles or grated block; fills approximately 12 tealight cups
pre-tabbed tealight wicks in aluminium cups; sized for standard 38 mm tealight cups

content.text: Arrange the 12 tealight cups on a flat tray. The pre-tabbed wicks sit centred in each cup on their aluminium tab.
Melt the beeswax in the pouring pitcher over a simmering-water bath. Never leave melting wax unattended. Bring to 75°C.
. Pour into each cup in a single, steady pour to just below the cup rim. Pour quickly, beeswax sets fast at tealight scale.
Leave on the tray undisturbed for 2 hours until fully set. If a small depression forms around the wick as the wax contracts, give a small top-up pour of melted wax at 70°C.
Trim the wicks to 3-4 mm before use.

Store in a box or tin in a cool, dry place. A white surface bloom is natural beeswax crystallisation, buff with a soft cloth. Beeswax tealights have no practical shelf limit; they improve with age as the wax hardens further.
